items.prompt:
When two organisms need the same limited resource, the interaction is:
A) Mutualism
B) Competition
C) Predation
D) Commensalism

steps: Needing the same limited resource is competition.

items.prompt:
Predation is when:
A) Both organisms benefit
B) One organism eats another
C) Organisms share equally
D) Nothing happens

In mutualism:
A) Both species benefit
B) Only one benefits and the other is harmed
C) Both are harmed
D) Nothing changes

A bee drinks nectar and pollinates the flower; both benefit. This is:
A) Parasitism
B) Competition
C) Mutualism
D) Predation

steps: Both benefit, so it is mutualism.

items.prompt:
A tick feeds on a dog's blood, harming the dog. This relationship is:
A) Mutualism
B) Commensalism
C) Parasitism
D) Competition

steps: One benefits and the other is harmed, which is parasitism.

items.prompt:
A bird builds a nest in a tree; the bird benefits and the tree is unaffected. This is:
A) Mutualism
B) Commensalism
C) Parasitism
D) Predation

steps: One benefits and the other is unaffected, which is commensalism.

items.prompt:
Why can a scientist predict how species will interact in an unfamiliar ecosystem?
A) Interactions are random
B) The same patterns of interaction repeat across ecosystems
C) Every ecosystem is totally unique
D) Species never interact
items.answer: B) The same patterns of interaction repeat across ecosystems

steps: Interaction patterns recur across ecosystems, allowing predictions.

items.prompt:
Which pair correctly matches a relationship to its outcome?
A) Parasitism: both benefit
B) Mutualism: one harmed
C) Commensalism: one benefits, other unaffected
D) Competition: both ignore each other
items.answer: C) Commensalism: one benefits, other unaffected

steps: In commensalism one benefits and the other is unaffected.
